scenario_interpretation: Analyst-defined adverse, base and favorable assumptions. These are not probability bounds, calibrated prediction intervals, management guidance or price targets. Outcomes can fall outside the range.
limits: A within-quarter fundamental forecast with no realized target-quarter outcome.
The forecast does not constitute full valuation, governance, cash-conversion or position-sizing underwriting.
Seasonal anchors use one prior year and can break when business mix changes.
rationale: Q1 PAT was lifted by other income of 8.9717cr versus 0.8850cr in Q2. Q2 revenue and EBIT support a base near the latest reported owner PAT, without assuming the Q1 income spike repeats. A simple seasonal forecast may be just as good.

verified_facts.fact: Q2 revenue 23.4148cr, other income 0.8850cr, finance cost 0.0373cr and PBT 9.1935cr.
Q1 other income was 8.9717cr. The reviewed statement does not establish that all of it is a one-time item.
Q2 owner PAT 6.8252cr differs from group PAT 6.8247cr because NCI is negative 0.0005cr. Q1 NCI is negative 0.0003cr.
Q2 tax comprises current 3.1372cr, deferred minus 0.8851cr and prior-period tax 0.1167cr, totaling 2.3688cr.

assumptions.label: Revenue
assumptions.basis: Approximately flat against Q2 and below the prior December quarter. No contract pipeline forecast was verified.

assumptions.label: EBIT margin
assumptions.basis: Below Q2 derived 35.64 percent to avoid treating one high margin as permanent.

assumptions.label: Other income
assumptions.basis: Near current Q2, without assuming Q1 spike repeats. This is a modeling choice, not a documented recurring-income run rate.

assumptions.label: Tax and NCI
assumptions.basis: Small normalized allowances. Current quarter negative NCI is not assumed indefinitely.

disconfirming_evidence_to_watch: Other income repeating close to Q1 rather than Q2 would make this base too low.
Revenue or personnel costs changing sharply would invalidate the assumed EBIT margin.
main_takeaway: The largest apparent sequential PAT decline is not evidence of an equally large deterioration in operating revenue.
